That is the opportunism. Guilt is not heritable. Charles was born in 1948. The men and women who captained the ships, bought the captives and worked the estates are dust. So are the African kings who captured them. The Kingdom of Dahomey ran a militarised slave economy and sold prisoners of war down to the coast at Ouidah for generations; Britain had to force it to stop in the 1850s. The Ashanti empire’s wealth rested on gold and slaves. Oyo, the coastal middlemen, the traders of the interior: the transatlantic trade did not begin when a European ship appeared on the horizon. It began when an African polity decided a neighbour was stock. The Arab and Muslim trade out of East Africa and across the Sahara ran longer and, on several serious counts, took more people. Nobody is invoicing Riyadh, Istanbul or the successors of Dahomey. The invoice is always presented in London, because London still pays, still feels awkward, and still has a public class that treats national self-accusation as a moral personality.

Britain’s actual record is the one the campaign has to blur. Parliament outlawed the British slave trade in 1807. It abolished slavery across most of the empire in 1833, freeing more than 760,000 people, and it paid the owners about £20 million to get the bill through. That sum was around 40 per cent of annual government expenditure and about 5 per cent of national output. Part of it was financed by undated gilts that were finally redeemed in 2015, which reparations lobbyists now wave as if the British public had been paying slave owners a secret stipend for 180 years. They were paying off a debt raised to end the institution. After 1807 the Royal Navy’s West Africa Squadron spent half a century intercepting the trade Britain had just made illegal for its own subjects. It took about 1,600 ships and freed about 150,000 Africans. Somewhere around 1,500 to 1,600 British sailors died on that station, mostly of disease. At its height the patrol cost on the order of 2 per cent of GDP. Portugal and Britain between them shipped more than 70 per cent of the transatlantic total, and Portugal shipped the larger share for long stretches. Spain kept the trade going later. The United States abolished slavery in 1865, by war. Britain did it by Act of Parliament, by cheque, and by naval blockade, earlier than almost anyone else with an empire. That is not the behaviour of a state that has a moral debt still outstanding in 2026. It is the behaviour of the state that closed the trade down and made other people hate it for doing so.

The legal trick is as cynical as the number. Slavery in the British Caribbean was lawful under the law of the time. International law did not then forbid it. A petition that asks a court in 2026 to declare an eighteenth-century statute a crime, and then to invent a duty to pay, is not jurisprudence. It is politics with a wig on. Jamaica cannot sue Britain at the International Court of Justice, which is why the route chosen is the Privy Council, a court that still exists because these same states have not yet cut the last constitutional string. They want the King as head of state to refer a case whose purpose is to extract money from the country of which he is also King. If he apologises in a formal, governmental sense, every lawyer on the circuit will treat the apology as an admission. That is why the apology is the point. Regret is free. An apology is a pleading.

The wider demands give the game away. CARICOM’s menu is not confined to a historical accounting. It includes debt cancellation, development assistance, healthcare funding and what they call decolonisation. Debt cancellation for loans taken out by independent governments in the late twentieth century has nothing to do with a barracoon in 1720. Healthcare funding is a budget bid. “Decolonisation” means republicanism, the removal of the Privy Council, and the symbolic humiliation of the Crown, after which the cash demand will still be there. Several of these countries have been independent for sixty years. Their murder rates, their governance failures, their emigration to the very country they are invoicing, are present-tense facts. Britain’s aid budgets, remittances from the British diaspora, and the open door of the NHS and the universities have transferred more wealth west-to-east since independence than the slave trade ever did in the other direction. None of that appears on the invoice.

This is the same caper the left, the Britain-haters and the woke have run for years, merely franchised. Take a real historical evil. Erase every actor who is not European. Erase the abolitionists, the sailors, the £20 million, the Squadron. Inflate a consultancy model until the number is too big to mean anything. Then present the refusal to pay as proof of ongoing guilt. At home the same people use it to indict the country that abolished the trade. Abroad, elites who cannot fix their own police forces, their own debts or their own schools get a permanent alibi and a claim on someone else’s treasury. The Commonwealth is treated not as a voluntary association but as a claims department.

The Palace has, for once, refused to play. The government, even this pathetic government, has said it will not pay and will not apologise. That is the correct answer, and it should be the last one. No formal apology. No referral that can be spun as an admission. No “non-cash reparatory justice” that turns into cash the moment the communiqué is signed. No seat at a table whose only agenda item is a bill for the dead, presented to people who were not alive, by governments that will not ask the same question of anyone else. The past was brutal. Britain ended its part in it at vast cost, in treasure and in lives, and then spent decades stopping other people from continuing it. That is the record. The rest is a caper.

text:
Sony Thang’s posts are rhetoric, not analysis. The method is the problem.
He treats every U.S. action as one pattern and every Chinese outcome as outside that pattern. Xinjiang, Taiwan, Tibet, the South China Sea, and the property bust never have to be explained. Washington calling China a threat is offered as proof China is not one. That is circular. States arm against rivals they trade with. The U.S. sold grain to the USSR and still contained it.
“America fell, China only held the mirror” skips the numbers. U.S. GDP is about $32 trillion to China’s $21 trillion. Output per person is roughly $90,000 versus $15,000. Unemployment is in the mid-4 percent range here. China’s home prices have fallen for about 37 straight months, property investment is down about 19 percent, youth unemployment is near 15 percent, and public debt including local financing vehicles is around 124 percent of GDP. A country in that shape is not the verdict on American decline.
The socialism point is missing entirely. China’s catch-up started when Deng dropped the command economy, not when the Party perfected it. Private firms, foreign capital, and export markets did the growing. The Party kept the banks, the land, and the political monopoly. Those are the parts now failing.
A list of U.S. interventions is not a theory of why Chinese households stopped spending, or why the dollar still clears the world’s trade.

في سوسيولوجيا الدين تمثل الماركسية ديانة علمانية وحسب الفيلسوف الابستمولوجي "كارل بوبر" أنها عقيدة دوغمائية وعلم زائف، نفس النتيجة عند فيلسوف العلم "ماريو بونجي" وعالم الاقتصاد "توماس سويل" الذي كان ماركسيا سابقا. في هذه الحلقة من دروس "Open College" التي يقدمها الحداثي الليبرالي "ستيفن هيكس" وأبرز نقاد الماركسية وما بعد الحداثة، نتعرف إلى السر الذي ما زال يجعل الاشتراكية تجذب أتباعًا بعد أكثر من قرن على دعوة كارل ماركس وفريدريك إنجلز للثورة الشيوعية عام 1848.

كان من أوائل مؤيدي الاشتراكية رجال دين، كالرهبان والراهبات على سبيل المثال. لكن ماركس وإنجلز قدّما ما أسمياه الاشتراكية العلمية. ومع ذلك، عند النظر إلى كتاباتهما، يتبادر إلى الذهن سؤال: هل هي حقًا قائمة على الحقائق والأدلة والحجج والتجارب، وعلى كامل منظومة العقل؟ أم أنها في نهاية المطاف نوع من الالتزام الإيماني؟

في النهاية، يُشبّه الدكتور هيكس رؤاهما المثالية بجنة عدن حديثة، ملحدة. ستيفن آر. سي. هيكس، الحاصل على درجة الدكتوراه، هو أستاذ الفلسفة في جامعة روكفورد بالولايات المتحدة الأمريكية، وقد شغل مناصب زائرة في جامعة جورج تاون في واشنطن العاصمة، وجامعة كازيمير العظيم في بولندا، وكلية هاريس مانشستر التابعة لجامعة أكسفورد في إنجلترا، وجامعة ياغيلونيا في بولندا.

- Socialism continues to attract followers more than a century after Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels first called for communist revolution in 1848.  Dr. Hicks sets out to investigate what is the attraction.

Early adherents of socialism were religious: monks and nuns, for instance.  But Marx and Engels offered what they called scientific socialism.  And yet, when you look at their writings, one has to ask: is it really based on facts, evidence, argumentation, experimentation, the whole apparatus of reason? Or is it ultimately a kind of faith commitment? 

In the end, Dr. Hicks likens their idealistic visions to a modernized, atheistic Garden of Eden.

For some time, Professor Hicks has been doing a philosophical analysis podcast on a wide range of contemporary topics.  It has been available on a number of other platforms.  It is now being offered on YouTube as well.  Its mission is to “ to explain the chaos.”

Stephen R. C. Hicks, Ph.D., is Professor of Philosophy at Rockford University, USA, and has had visiting positions at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C., University of Kasimir the Great in Poland, Oxford University’s Harris Manchester College in England, and Jagiellonian University in Poland.

text:
🇸🇻 THIS WEEK IN EL SALVADOR | VOL. 15
⠀
SEPTEMBER 26 – OCTOBER 3, 2026
⠀
A WEEK OF ECONOMIC MOMENTUM
⠀
5.1% economic growth. A stock market up 38.6%. IMF approval. Construction financing exceeding $1.62 billion. Growing exports. International tourism recognition.
⠀
And in the heart of San Salvador, a historic tribute to the man who dreamed of a united Central America.
⠀
This week brought together economic results, international confidence, investment, innovation, security and national history.
⠀
Here are the developments shaping El Salvador.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
1. THE IMF APPROVES $138 MILLION AS EL SALVADOR'S ECONOMY EXCEEDS EXPECTATIONS
⠀
One of the week's most significant announcements came from Washington.
⠀
On October 1, the International Monetary Fund's Executive Board completed the second and third reviews of its financing arrangement with El Salvador, allowing an immediate disbursement of approximately $138 million.
⠀
The IMF reported that economic activity had exceeded expectations, supported by sustained improvements in security and growing investor confidence.
⠀
It also recognized progress in fiscal consolidation, financial resilience and the strengthening of liquidity and reserve buffers.
⠀
The approval represents an important milestone in El Salvador's $1.4 billion financing arrangement.
⠀
For international investors, the IMF's assessment provides another reference point when evaluating the country's economic direction.
⠀
The bigger story is the convergence of stronger economic performance, international financing and growing investment interest.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
2. EL SALVADOR'S ECONOMY GROWS 5.1%
⠀
The Central Reserve Bank reported that El Salvador's economy expanded 5.1% during the second quarter of 2026.
⠀
That compares with 4.1% growth during the corresponding period of 2025.
⠀
Construction, healthcare and electricity were among the principal drivers.
⠀
A separate economic activity indicator showed growth of 4.5% in July, with construction continuing to make an important contribution.
⠀
These figures help explain why the construction industry has become one of the central stories in our recent weekly editions.
⠀
Investment is increasingly visible in the country's economic indicators and its changing urban landscape.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
3. EL SALVADOR'S STOCK MARKET SURGES 38.6%
⠀
Another major financial indicator arrived this week.
⠀
According to figures published by the Financial System Superintendency, trading activity on the Salvadoran stock exchange reached $4.483 billion between January and August 2026.
⠀
That represents an increase of 38.6% compared with the same period in 2025.
⠀
The market registered 4,827 transactions during those eight months.
⠀
International securities transactions accounted for approximately $1.449 billion, while investment funds reported total assets of approximately $2.216 billion.
⠀
Meanwhile, the integrated stock market connecting El Salvador and Panama recorded $165.3 million in transactions.
⠀
These figures illustrate the increasing activity and regional connections of El Salvador's capital markets.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
4. CONSTRUCTION FINANCING EXCEEDS $1.62 BILLION
⠀
The country's construction expansion is also reflected in bank lending.
⠀
Loans associated with construction exceeded $1.62 billion through August.
⠀
Housing, land development and commercial infrastructure accounted for approximately 97% of that financing portfolio.
⠀
Another indicator reinforces the picture.
⠀
Construction-related imports surpassed $1.13 billion during the first eight months of 2026.
⠀
The relationship between financing and material imports helps illustrate the scale of activity underway.
⠀
Following last week's announcements involving Paseo Vivo, Reforma 150 and San Benito 53, these figures provide broader economic context for the projects transforming metropolitan San Salvador and other parts of the country.
⠀
@LRodriguez_SV, Executive Director of the San Salvador Metropolitan Area Planning Office (@COAMSS_OPAMSS), has been highlighting the investment momentum behind this construction expansion. His involvement in the recently announced Paseo Vivo development in Apopa illustrates how the institution is helping facilitate new projects and attract investment to areas benefiting from improved security conditions.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
5. BUSINESS DELEGATIONS FROM 21 COUNTRIES EXPLORE EL SALVADOR
⠀
El Salvador's economic diplomacy continues opening international doors.
⠀
According to reporting published this week, business delegations representing 21 countries have visited El Salvador to explore commercial and investment opportunities.
⠀
The initiative reflects an international outreach strategy focused on attracting businesses, expanding commercial relationships and presenting opportunities in the Salvadoran market.
⠀
Combined with the latest economic results and IMF developments, these international contacts form another part of the country's investment story.
⠀
The challenge ahead is converting business interest into completed investments, jobs and long-term economic activity.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
6. EXPORTS REACH $4.529 BILLION
⠀
El Salvador exported approximately $4.529 billion in goods between January and August 2026.
⠀
Central America and the United States remained its principal commercial partners, together accounting for 81.1% of total exports.
⠀
Food products were identified as one of the most dynamic export categories.
⠀
Another report highlighted El Salvador's regional performance in export sophistication, reflecting the ability of Salvadoran companies to manufacture and commercialize increasingly diversified products.
⠀
The importance extends beyond total export values.
⠀
Industrial capabilities, product development and access to international markets help determine how Salvadoran businesses can compete and expand.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
7. WORLD TOURISM DAY COMES TO EL SALVADOR
⠀
El Salvador hosted World Tourism Day 2026, marking the first time the country welcomed this international event organized under the United Nations tourism framework.
⠀
Tourism Minister @MorenaValdezSV highlighted the country's international recognition for tourism growth.
⠀
Figures reported during the week placed El Salvador's tourism growth at approximately 37% during the referenced reporting period.
⠀
The international event provided an opportunity to present El Salvador's destinations, tourism development and growing international visibility.
⠀
Tourism also connects directly with other recurring themes in our reports: security, aviation, hospitality investment, infrastructure and employment.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
8. FRANCISCO MORAZÁN: HONORING A DREAM OF CENTRAL AMERICAN UNITY
⠀
October 3 marked the 234th anniversary of the birth of General Francisco Morazán.
⠀
This year's commemoration carried special historical significance.
⠀
For the first time, the ceremony took place at his newly inaugurated mausoleum in Jardín Centroamérica, beside the National Palace in San Salvador.
⠀
Government officials, members of the diplomatic corps, military personnel and citizens participated in the commemorative activities.
⠀
The ceremony included military honors, cannon salutes, a floral offering, the Salvadoran national anthem and an aerial display.
⠀
Defense Minister @merino_monroy emphasized Morazán's commitment to a cause that extended beyond national borders: Central American unity.
⠀
The new mausoleum, inaugurated following President @nayibbukele's initiative, places Morazán's remains in the heart of San Salvador's revitalized Historic Center.
⠀
It also creates a public space dedicated to remembering his life and political ideals.
⠀
More than a historical monument, the new mausoleum offers future generations an opportunity to discover the story of a leader who devoted his life to the vision of a united Central America.
⠀
His dream remains an important part of the region's shared history.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
9. OCTOBER BEGINS WITH TWO HOMICIDE-FREE DAYS
⠀
El Salvador entered October with two consecutive days without homicides, according to figures released by the National Civil Police.
⠀
October 1 and October 2 were both reported as homicide-free.
⠀
The official figures brought the country's accumulated total to 235 homicide-free days during 2026 through October 2.
⠀

text:
Travel pool report #4: Rally departure

POTUS took the stage at 7:45 pm to a standing ovation. He ended at 9:17 pm with the “YMCA” dance.

Some highlights for you to check against transcripts:

- The president again asked people to pretend he is on the ballot: “I’m really in to win it. We want to win the midterm … If you don’t mind please pretend that I’m on the ballot.”

- People stood up and cheered when he offered $5000 checks if Republicans keep control of Congress. Near the end of the rally he brought it up again, and several people clapped and jumped up and down.

- A protester was escorted out shortly after the president began talking.

- There was thunderous applause for a Voter ID measure on the Ohio ballot; for POTUS saying that zero undocumented immigrants have been admitted across the border; and for his support for barring transgender people from women’s sports.

- John Husted got applause when the president highlighted his attempts to get legislation passed that the president said would stop data centers from driving up utility costs.

- People began streaming out from an upper deck and seats along the side of the auditorium once the speech hit the 45-minute mark. Around that point, the president read the poem The Snake and dedicated it to the town of Springfield Ohio

- He pondered the future: “I’ll try a couple of years of being nonconsequential if you don’t mind. This is a dangerous position.”

- “I had a simple life before this. He said that he didn’t have to be here on a Saturday night“working my ass off.” “I could’ve been in Monte Carlo!” At that, the president received a standing ovation and a “four more years” chat. He said he’d “like to do that” but then complained that the news media would report that he wanted to run again.

- He disparaged polls showing dimming prospects for Republicans as fake, and said the polls have not taken into account the fact that he is now campaigning. “It’s their fault because they’ve unleashed us.”

- He invited Husted onstage. Husted got a standing ovation when he said this week Ohio reported the lowest unemployment rate in the history of Ohio.

- He invited Ramaswamy onstage, and he said he was running against the “Kamala Harris of Ohio.” His challenger’s name is Amy Acton. The president called her a “radical left lunatic.”

- The president thanked Bill Pulte for attending and someone in the crowd yelled out “Wild Bill Pulte!”

- He said “the Golden Age is upon us but you must get out and vote Republican.”

- He seemed happy to see “Mr Wall” of his diehard Front Row Joes fan club. He said “in my final appearance I’m going to put a jacket on like that,” gesturing to the man’s brick wall-print suit.

Also of note: The president’s motorcade was rerouted to the venue initially due to the protest outside, per a USSS official.

Thanks to Haley Bull & Elyse Perlmutter for catching a few of these things.

Pool was ushered out while the president was still onstage and interacting with fans behind him.

Rolling to airport at 9:23 pm.

Katie Rogers
The New York Times
Sat. Oct. 3, 9:27 PM

On October 3, former Yokozuna Hakuho took part in harvesting sake rice in Gokokuji-machi, Komatsu City. Under the watchful eye of Naohiko Noguchi, who is recognized as a holder of Ishikawa Prefecture's Intangible Cultural Heritage for Sake Brewing Master, Hakuho worked alongside local residents, expressing his hopes: "It is a joy to be involved in sake making with Mr. Noguchi, whom I have respected since my active days. I hope a delicious sake comes out of this."

At the rice paddy where he had participated in rice planting in late April, Hakuho held a sickle and harvested stalks of "Yamada Nishiki" rice one after another. Receiving advice from local farmers, he also operated a combine harvester to bring in the harvest across an area of approximately 1,000 square meters.

Speaking to reporters after the harvest, Hakuho commented on Yokozuna Onosato, who secured his first tournament victory in a year at the Aki Basho: "Only the wrestler himself understands the fight against injury, but I think he fought very hard." Regarding his former disciple Enho, who narrowly ended up with a losing record in the Juryo division, he offered words of encouragement: "It was unfortunate, but I hope he bounces back in the next tournament."
